newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch says GDP data validate Treasury f'casts.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch says GDP data validate Treasury f'casts.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Friday that June quarter GDP data validated Treasury forecasts showing growth climbing again to 3.7 percent in 1997/98, 3.0 percent in 1998/99 and 3.5 percent in 1999/2000.
The Treasury forecasts, released earlier this month, were higher than private sector and Reserve Bank forecasts.
Birch said the actual annual growth of 2.6 percent in production-based GDP was positive news and fully in line with business expectations.
"At the bottom of the current business cycle, New Zealand is likely to be achieving more than twice its average rate of growth in the 15 years to 1991," he said in a statement.

"The 2.6 percent annual growth shown in today's results will improve public confidence in the ability of the economy to move forward successfully next year into further improved non-inflationary growth."
Production-based GDP rose by a seasonally-adjusted 0.3 percent in the June quarter, versus economists' average forecasts of 0.4 percent.
